utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Nice and easy. Hold the thread.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That sounds pretty fast to me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Is that straight? Man, that seam is so clean!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Clean? Did you spill something on the fabric, dear? I don't see any dirt. Let me get the damp cloth from the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: No, no, Grandma! Stay here. 'Clean' just means the line is perfect. It looks professional.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh! You young people and your words. I thought I'd have to start scrubbing the cotton. If it’s straight, just say it’s straight!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yeah, you got a little wide there at the end. Okay, let's do this again. It's gonna make a difference. You see how you went big?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That— it— like I said, it doesn't seem like a lot, but it does make a difference in the end. Your corners won't match up. Quilters always say, "Quarter inch is my friend." All right. Okay, I think the top one was good. No, that's all right. Drop the foot, hold the thread. Okay, go back, backtrack.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Okay, go front. Off the material. Okay. There, that's better. All right, let me iron this up.
